newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Delhi stocks closed lower in thin trading on Tuesday as foreign and domestic financial institutions reduced their positions and speculators booked profits, brokers said.
The end of settlement on the National Stock Exchange and lower trends in the Bombay market triggered selling pressure.
Unit Trust of India (UTI), India's largest mutual fund, sold big quantities of blue chipes including State Bank of India and ACC, pushing down prices, brokers said.
The benchmark index dropped 7.80 points to close at 786.36.

"Selling in heavy weighted stocks by FIIs (foreign institutional investors) which had bought the shares in the post-budget rally gave an opportunity to bearish speculators to regain charge," said B. K. Nagpal of brokers B.B. Portfolio.
"The market may dip further as speculative buying has been drying up gradually," said another broker.
Reliance dropped 6.65 rupees to 279 on selling by speculators and mutual funds after rising to 290.25 in early trade.
ACC closed 67 rupees lower at 1,659 after spurting to 1,760 at mid-session.
